bad.title: Three settings behind a vague label
bad.text: Send later, priority and read receipt all sit here, and the button names none of them.

bad.title: Send later was here all along
bad.text: Someone who wants it sent tomorrow at 8:00 only finds out by opening the box.
bad.wait: Press More options to see this.

good.title: The button lists what’s inside
good.text: “Send later” is on the label, so people know it exists before they open anything.

good.title: Inside matches the label
good.text: The three switches are the three names on the button, nothing more.
good.wait: Press the More options button to see this.

bad.title: Closed again for every photo
bad.text: Advanced (2) folds shut after each Export, so every photo costs one more click.

bad.title: The click count keeps climbing
bad.text: Five photos with Advanced each time means five extra clicks.

good.title: Stays open once it’s opened
good.text: Open Advanced once and it’s still open for the next photo.

good.title: Always show, or press Alt+A
good.text: People who change these every time can skip the button for good.

good.title: One click covers all five photos
good.text: Clicks on Advanced stays at 1, however many photos people export.

bad.title: Four options, one that people need
bad.text: More options (4) hides the video call among settings few people touch.

bad.title: The split saves almost nobody a click
bad.text: Opened in 82% of events, so nearly every new event pays the extra click.

good.title: Add video call sits in the basics
good.text: The one switch most people change is right under When.

good.title: Three options few people touch
good.text: Busy for others, Private and Color stay tucked away.

good.title: Hidden is now the rare case
good.text: At 6% of events, the extra click costs almost nobody anything.

bad.title: Filters looks like nothing is on
bad.text: The button reads the same with or without last week’s Under €20 filter.

bad.title: One lamp, and no reason why
bad.text: Only the €18 clip-on lamp shows. Three others are filtered out of sight.

good.title: Under €20 shows beside Filters
good.text: People see the filter that’s on without opening anything, and the × clears it.

good.title: One result, with the cause in view
good.text: The chip above explains why only the €18 lamp is left.

bad.title: Starts on a size few people want
bad.text: Twelve summer photos rarely go on passports, so people change Size first.

bad.title: Fixed by hand on every order
bad.text: Order 13 × 18 cm twice and the count reads 2, because Size snaps back to Passport.

good.title: Starts on 10 × 15 cm
good.text: The size most people order needs no change at all.

good.title: The reason, in words
good.text: “Most people pick this” says why the size is already chosen, and turns into “Your last size” later.

good.title: One change, then remembered
good.text: Order 13 × 18 cm twice and the count stays at 1.

bad.title: 6000 × 4000, and no size setting
bad.text: Nothing on the form hints that the photo will be shrunk.

bad.title: 2048 × 1365 in the album
bad.text: People find out after the upload, and the full-size photo isn’t there.

good.title: Reduce to 2048 px, in plain view
good.text: People see the default and can pick Original size before uploading.

good.title: Changed, marked in words
good.text: The edit reads the same without color, so nobody misses it.
good.wait: Pick Original size to see this.

good.title: The result matches the form
good.text: 2048 × 1365, as the form said. Nothing comes as a surprise.

bad.title: Public is ticked from the start
bad.text: Kids at the beach goes to anyone with the link unless people spot the box.

bad.title: Kids’ photos, public by default
bad.text: One press on Create album, and people outside their contacts can see them.
bad.wait: Press Create album to see this.

good.title: Starts private, sharing is opt-in
good.text: Nothing leaves people’s contacts unless they tick the box themselves.

good.title: Private now, shared when ready
good.text: “Only you can see it,” and sharing stays one tick away.
good.wait: Press Create album to see this.

bad.title: Gray text that looks filled in
bad.text: “2 people” is only a placeholder, so people skip the field.

bad.title: Refused for an empty field
bad.text: Book fails on a field people thought they had answered.

good.title: 2 people is already chosen
good.text: A real value, so Book works without touching the field.

good.title: Booked on the first press
good.text: A table for 2 on Friday at 19:30, with no error first.

bad.title: Three names, no values
bad.text: Eco, Comfort and Away say nothing about the temperatures they set.

bad.title: 17 °C an hour later
bad.text: People learn what Eco does only when the room gets cold.

good.title: Day, night and away temperatures
good.text: Eco shows 18 °C, 16 °C and Off before the house cools down.

good.title: Every value can be edited
good.text: Someone who wants 19 °C by day types it in and keeps the rest of Eco.

bad.title: Still says Focus: Sleep
bad.text: Calls from Everyone isn’t Sleep anymore, but the phone says it is.
bad.wait: Set Calls from to Everyone to see this.

bad.title: Sleep stays picked
bad.text: Nothing marks the edit, so people later trust Sleep to block calls.
bad.wait: Set Calls from to Everyone to see this.

good.title: Custom, based on Sleep
good.text: The status line says what’s on and where it came from.
good.wait: Set Calls from to Everyone to see this.

good.title: Custom takes over the selection
good.text: Sleep is no longer picked, and picking it again brings its values back.
good.wait: Set Calls from to Everyone to see this.

good.title: Edited marks the changed row
good.text: People see exactly which value differs from Sleep.
good.wait: Set Calls from to Everyone to see this.

bad.title: Twelve codes like JPG-80-2048
bad.text: People have to decode format, quality and size just to email three photos.

bad.title: A size in MB, but no answer
bad.text: 4.1 MB still doesn’t say whether it fits an email or opens on Grandma’s tablet.

good.title: Four choices, one per purpose
good.text: Email, Web, Print and Original cover what people do with photos.

good.title: Each one says what it’s for
good.text: “Small, fits in any email” answers the question people came with.

good.title: 1.8 MB, opens anywhere
good.text: Picking Email confirms Grandma can open the photos on any device.

bad.title: Cheapest and Fastest, nothing else
bad.text: Neither one is Nonstop plus Under €150, the mix people want.

bad.title: Set by hand on every route
bad.text: New search clears all four filters, so the same taps start over.

bad.title: The count only goes up
bad.text: Two taps per route adds up to eight for four routes.

good.title: My usual sits beside the built-in ones
good.text: One tap brings back Nonstop and Under €150 on any route.
good.wait: Turn on Nonstop and Under €150, then press Save as preset to see this.

good.title: Save as preset keeps the mix
good.text: It turns on once a filter is set and saves exactly those filters.

good.title: The count stops at 2
good.text: After saving, New search and My usual skip the taps.
